detail.body:
The SM100 BF16 D128 paged-prefix selector currently excludes 128-token pages even though the same split kernels support them. Admit page sizes 16 and 128 to the existing occupancy-based split/packing choice. This lets eligible underfilled page128 graphs consider the same default split route as page16 graphs; the existing shape, mask, layout, batch and workspace constraints still apply.

This is a one-line selector change. Kernel implementations, prepared execution, workspace layout and the SM107 page16-only selection domain are unchanged. It is independent of #1709 and does not expand FlashInfer auto admission.

Validation:
- Existing heuristic/geometry suites: 1,155 passed, 2 deselected.
- Existing BF16 page128 dynamic-length, pointer-rebinding, O/LSE and CUDA Graph tests: 42 passed.
- Ten-shape baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline component matrix passed O/LSE, sampled fp64 and poisoned-output replay checks; an additional six-shape output-only FA2/FA4/TRTLLM comparison passed correctness.
- Scoped pre-commit checks passed. No timing or winning-knob golden tests added.

Ready for review. Full-power B200 performance qualification and remote CI remain prerequisites for merging; local component measurements do not establish a serving-wide default-dispatch win.

files.patch:
@@ -2547,7 +2547,7 @@ def paged_thd_split_choice(caps: Capabilities, facts) -> Tuple[int, bool]:
         and facts.h_kv > 0
         and facts.h_q % facts.h_kv == 0
         and facts.h_q // facts.h_kv in ((1, 2, 4, 8, 16) if caps.sm_lo == 100 else (1, 2, 4, 8))
-        and facts.page_size == 16
+        and facts.page_size in ((16, 128) if caps.sm_lo == 100 else (16,))
         and facts.causal
         and facts.bottom_right
         and facts.window_left is None

B200 default-selection qualification is now complete for `51ea7c58c68f`: base/head/head/base, 1000 W B200, cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CuTe DSL 4.8.0, CUDA 13.2, fresh matching bindings and verified loaded-library paths.

The ten-shape page128 matrix exercised ordinary and graph-mode FlashInfer wrappers with O/Stats, full numerical checks, sampled fp64 references and poisoned-output replay. All 120 timed measurements passed. Eight shapes switch from backend to the existing FROST implementation and improve warm GPU replay by 17–87%; two control shapes retain backend, with at most +0.26% warm-replay difference.

Representative ordinary-wrapper results (BF16 D128, page128):

| B, Hq/Hkv, Q, KV | Old default → new default |
|---|---:|
| 1, 8/1, 64, 2048 | 42.48 → 15.05 µs |
| 1, 16/4, 128, 8192 | 160.51 → 22.36 µs |
| 1, 32/8, 512, 8192 | 107.86 → 79.92 µs |
| 4, 16/4, 256 each, 8192 each | 107.52 → 89.17 µs |

The provider switch has an eager-host cost: enqueue increases about 4–8 µs on those ordinary-wrapper cases. The selector adds no per-run preparation; this is the existing split FROST execution path replacing backend. GPU replay improves, but I am not claiming the host path is free or that FI auto should unconditionally select cuDNN. FI page128 auto admission is unchanged. The corrected output-only cross-provider comparison is also complete: all 24 measurements passed numerical, sampled-fp64 and poisoned-replay checks, with exact library paths verified. These use the same ordinary-wrapper workload tensors, FA4 at vLLM's pinned source, and the public TRTLLM context API with `lse=None`; they are component timings, not serving results. cuDNN wins 3/6 cases, so selective admission remains necessary.

The scoped GPU benefit is reproduced locally; retain the distinction between replay gains, eager-host cost and serving-wide admission.

Validation: 1,203 heuristic, geometry and placement tests passed. Native SM100 with DSL 4.7.0 used verified source imports and compatible matching bindings. Three HND page128 shapes passed full FP64 O/LSE checks, changed-length retained CUDA Graph replay, empty/causal-empty rows, poisoned outputs and untouched-tail checks. NHD controls preserved the original route. The three HND cases also passed on an isolated integration with current base ae7493d2, including #1709. Base/head/head/base, using each graph's first FROST candidate without knob overrides: B1 Hq8/Hkv2 Q64/KV4096 changed split1 to split8 and measured 94.46 to 26.89 us; B3 Hq16/Hkv1 Q129/KV8192 changed to packed split4 and measured 350.53 to 123.30 us. A filled B4 MHA control remained unsplit at 69.11 to 69.58 us (+0.68%). CPU enqueue paired means increased 25.71 to 31.39 us and 28.75 to 32.40 us, with 25.25 to 27.58 us on the unchanged control; host variance contributes. All reference/replay checks passed in each fresh process. Read the author's B200 wrapper qualification and failure attribution in [this update](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1710#issuecomment-6250065201), kept distinct from my local execution. Reused current-head pipeline 74796874: 23 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped, 11 manual; the changed source matches its integration tree. SDPA SM80/100/103/120 and C++ sanitizer lanes passed.

Limitations: The local bounded SM100 timing is not independent B200 or end-to-end serving qualification; clocks were not locked. I did not independently run SM107. SM107 and guardwords remain failed CI jobs. The author attributes them to the baseline dense-D64 sink/SWA route assertion and an unchanged normalization README URL respectively; I have not independently inspected their raw traces.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
